Commentary.Commentary: So, that is it from this game and this series! It is Mahmudullah's side who comes out on top, yes they did lose the final game but have won the series. We hope you enjoyed our coverage. If you have not had enough of cricket, you can switch tabs and catch all the action from the ongoing T20I between Sri Lanka and South Africa. Until next time, take care and goodbye!

Mahmudullah, the Bangladesh skipper, says that he would have liked to won the game but credits the opposition on how they played. Says that the bowlers did well but they did not finish well and gave away some runs. Adds that he and Afif tried to stitch a partnership but their opposition's bowlers did well. He hopes to go to the World Cup and win games there too.
Tom Latham and Nasum Ahmed will share the PLAYER OF THE SERIES AWARD!

Tom Latham, New Zealand skipper and MAN OF THE MATCH, says it is great to finish on a high. They took all the learnings from the last games and played well here. Adds the way Finn played at the start helped them take their own time in the middle and they finished it well at the back end. States it was good they could finish the leg on a high and they will hope they can take the momentum forward in the next tour. Ends by saying that tour is another opportunity for the young guys and they are looking forward to the series.
... TIME FOR THE PRESENTATION ...

Earlier in the day, after electing to bat, Allen got the Kiwis off to a flier. Bangladesh did crawl back into the game courtesy of a few wickets but Latham, with a half ton, helped his side finish strongly and took them to a score which was above par and defended it easily.

For Bangladesh, the problem was there was a minimal contribution from the top order. Early wickets just pushed them well behind in the game. Mahmudullah and Afif Hossain did bring back the belief but the task was an uphill one. Afif Hossain was brilliant. Had the top order played better, the story could have well been different.

Their batters did their job in the first half and the bowlers did not disappoint. They were really good in the Powerplay as they did not let the runs flow and also managed to get a wicket. After that, they kept squeezing which saw the pressure building on the Bangladesh batters which eventually resulted in wickets. There was a period in between where they were put under a little pressure but they kept their calm and ensured their side finish on top. All the bowlers had a wicket at least to their name and everybody had a good day at the office, however, one has to say, Ajaz Patel was the pick.
A really good win for the visitors! A convincing win and they end the series on a high! They have completely outplayed the hosts in both the departments in this final game.
A full ball, on middle. Ahmed pushes it down to long on and takes a couple. New Zealand win by 27 runs.
A slower full ball, way outside off. Ahmed misses his drive.
A pacy short ball, on middle, it nips back in. Afif Hossain looks to defend but gets some gloves on it as the ball rolls away to the off side. Single taken.
Short in length, on middle, pulled away to deep square leg for two.
A length ball, on middle. Ahmed turns it to the wide of long on for a single.
On the pads, this is flicked to mid-wicket for a single.
Nasum Ahmed is the new man in.

OUT! TIMBER! Scott Kuggeleijn gets his second! A full ball, on middle. Taskin Ahmed clears his front leg and looks to heave it on the leg side but fails to get any bat on it. The ball sneaks through and disturbs the stumps behind.
FOUR! Consolation runs! A full ball, on middle. Ahmed makes room and hammers it straight down the ground for a boundary.
Very full and on middle. Afif pushes it to mid off for a single.
On a length, on middle, worked on the off side for a single.
FOUR! A full ball, on off. Ahmed lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Short and on middle. Hossain goes for the pull but ends up splicing it to the vacant cover region. A single taken.
Taskin Ahmed walks out.

OUT! BOWLED! Hossain is done in here by the slower delivery. A length ball, slower and on middle. Hossain clears his front leg and looks to play across the line but gets beaten by the pace and the ball sneaks through and rattles the stumps.
Angles a short ball, on middle. Hossain misses his pull shot.
On a length, on off, pushed through covers for a single.
A yorker-length ball, outside off. Hossain fails to dig it out.
Very full and outside off. Afif steps across and looks to paddle scoop but fails to get any bat on it.
Angles a length ball, on off, tucked to mid-wicket for a single.
Very full and outside off. Hossain turns it across the line towards mid-wicket for a single.
A full ball, on middle. Blocked out.
Review time! Bangladesh have taken a review for LBW. Ball Tracker shows three reds and Nurul Hasan is a goner.

OUT! LBW! A full ball, around leg, it lands and spins away from the right-hander. Nurul Hasan gets on his knee and looks to sweep but gets beaten by the spin and gets rapped on the pads. An appeal and up goes the finger. Hasan takes the review. UltraEdge shows no bat. Ball Tracker shows three reds and Bangladesh lose their review. The game is now slipping away.
FOUR! Nicely played! A full ball, angling down. Hasan makes room and lofts it through covers for a boundary.
Touch short, outside off. Hasan looks to cut but fails to connect it.
A flatter ball, on off, pushed to point.
Nurul Hasan walks out. Also, Ajaz Patel is back on.

OUT! TAKEN! New Zealand needed this wicket badly and they have found the breakthrough. A full ball, way outside off. Mahmudullah gets tempted for the widish delivery and looks to loft it over covers. He hits it but does not middle it. Finds Finn Allen in the deep who takes a simple catch. Bangladesh needed this pair to go on. Afif now will have to do bulk of the scoring as it is not easy for the new batter to come in and go for it straightaway.
Commentary.Howout: c Finn Allen b Scott Kuggeleijn

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on off, worked on the off side for a single.
A short ball, on off. Afif looks to pull but gets cramped for the room.
A length ball, on middle. Mahmudullah looks to pull but gets an inside edge back on the pads. The ball lobs on the leg side and they scamper across for a quick single.
Short and on middle. Mahmudullah looks to pull but gets beaten by the pace.
On a length, on off. Hossain guides it to third man for a single.
Full toss, on the bodyline, swept away to square leg for a single. 56 needed of 30 balls.
Angles it outside off, a fuller ball. Afif Hossain looks to guide it down the ground but fails to connect it.
A full ball, on middle. Blocked out.
SIX! 13 already of the over! Drags his length back a bit, on off. Afif Hossain gets on his knee and slogs it all the way over mid-wicket for a biggie.
FOUR! Runs are flowing nicely for Bangladesh now! A full ball, around off. Afif Hossain hits it straight down the ground for a boundary.
Angles it on the leg stump. Mahmudullah makes room and cuts it to point for a single.
SIX! Afif joins the party now! Another huge hit! A huge over and Bangladesh back in it. 68 needed in 36! Shorter and on the body, it is pulled over the square leg fence for a biggie.
Well fielded! Shorter and outside off, this is slapped but the fielder at covers dives to his right and stops it.
Shorter and outside off, Mahmudullah lofts it over cover for one.
SIX! BANG! That is huge! This time Mahmudullah connects with the slog sweep, the line is a lot straighter, it is nailed over the mid-wicket fence for a welcome biggie.

Chance not taken again! Afif looks to play the reverse sweep but this way too full, he jams it out to covers. Mahmudullah wants a run, Afif does not, Mahmudullah continues to run towards him. Afif then goes for it. The throw is towards the bowler who does not collect the ball.

DROPPED! Not the easiest of chances! This is tossed up outside off, Mahmudullah shuffles across and looks to play the slog sweep, it goes off the top edge towards mid-wicket. The bowler runs after it and then puts in a dive but the ball does not stay in. A single taken.

Just over! Shorter again and outside off, Afif cuts, it goes just over point. They take two. Mahmudullah wants the third and sets off, the batter does not spot that, he does so late but by the time he thinks of going for it, Mahmudullah turns and heads back to the non-striker's end.
Shorter and outside off, Afif guides it to point.
Flatter and on off, this is pushed through covers for one.
Fuller and on off, this is hit down to long off for one.
Safe! Mahmudullah now plays the reverse sweep, it goes off the glove and lobs over the keeper for one.
FOUR! 18 from the last 7 balls! On the pads, this is swept nicely past short fine leg for a boundary.
SIX! BANG! This is the kind of over Bangladesh needed, 14 from it. Is this the start of something for the hosts? A full ball on the pads, this is whipped over the square leg fence for a biggie.
Shortish but down the leg side, wided.
FOUR! Up and over! That is a lovely stroke! Fuller and outside off, Afif lifts it over covers for a boundary. They need a lot more.
Hits it well but only for one! Shorter and on middle, Mahmudullah pulls it hard through mid-wicket for one.
Another good short one, a slower short one. Mahmudullah looks to pull but is done in by the lack of pace.
On middle, this is worked towards mid on for one.
On the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
Shorter and on middle, this is nudged on the leg side for one.
Extra bounce saves Mahmudullah! He moves to his right and then tries to play the slog sweep, the length is dragged back. Mahmudullah misses and it goes over the middle pole.
Two! On middle, Mahmudullah works it with soft hands through mid-wicket and takes two.
Shorter and on the body, Afifi pulls, it goes more off the splice towards deep square leg for one.
Shorter and outside off, this is played through point for one.
Cheeky! Plays the reverse paddle scoop, it goes nice and fine on the off side for three.
Another single as this is played through covers.
Outside off, fuller. Afif had made a lot of room and hence, he leaves it alone as he knew he would not be able to reach it.
One more slower one, it is worked through square leg for one.
Really good bowling! Another slower one on off, it is played to mid off.
Slightly shorter and outside off, Mahmudullah looks to pull but this one stays low again and it is another dot.
Good length and on off, stays a touch low. Blocked.
Sees Hossain come down the track. Ravindra bowls it full and on the pads. Hossain misses his flick and gets hit on the pads.

OUT! TAKEN! Another one bites the dust and Ravindra gets a wicket to his name. Tosses this one up, around off, gives a bit of flight to this. Mushfiqur Rahim makes room and looks to go inside out but ends up chipping it in the air and towards wide of long off where Colin de Grandhomme takes a simple catch.  MAHMUDULLAH is the new man in.
Commentary.Howout: c Colin de Grandhomme b Rachin Ravindra

Commentary.Commentary: A full ball, on off, driven through covers for a single.
A touch fuller, on off. Rahim lofts it towards long off for a single.
A tossed up ball, on middle, kept out.
A full ball, on off, pushed to covers.
Now a slower ball, on middle, Rahim nudges it to square leg for one.118 needed in 72 balls.
WIDE! Full and angling down the leg side. Rahim misses his flick. Wided.
On a length, on middle, dabbed to third man for a single.
Full and on middle, tucked to square leg for one more.
Darted on the pads. Hossain flicks it to deep square leg for a single. He is off the mark.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Pace does the trick for Sears, 147.1 kmph! A full ball, way outside off. Naim leans and goes for a big booming drive but ends up edging it to the keeper. Tom Latham behind the sticks takes a good catch. New Zealand right on the top here.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Latham b Ben Sears

Commentary.Commentary: Good pace and bounce from Sears! A short of a length, around off. Naim looks to poke but fails to get any bat on it.
A flatter ball, on off. Rahim nudges it on the leg side. 123 needed in 78 balls.
Darted on the pads, Rahim tucks it to square leg.
WIDE! Spills it down the leg side. Wided.
Has that been taken? Sarkar is walking off. It is taken upstairs.

OUT! TAKEN! Brilliant catch by Rachin Ravindra. A flatter ball, outside off, the ball skids off the surface. Soumya Sarkar gets low to cut it but does it off the outer half of his bat to point. Rachin Ravindra standing inside the ring, puts a full stretched forward dive to grab it. They take it upstairs to check but replays show that is as clean as a whistle. Mushfiqur Rahim is the new man in.
Commentary.Howout: c Rachin Ravindra b Cole McConchie

Commentary.Commentary: On middle, Naim turns it to square leg for a single.
A full ball, on off. Sarkar lofts it to long off for one.
A full ball, on off, pushed through covers for a single.
Around off, on a length, pushed down to long on for a single. End of the Powerplay, Bangladesh are 35 for 1.
FOUR! Good shot! A length ball, outside off. Naim drags his pull from outside off towards square leg for a boundary.
Pitches it up, on middle. Sarkar mistimes his loft, over the bowler's head. The mid off fielder cuts it off. Single taken.
Touch short, on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
A length ball, outside off. Naim guides it to third man for a single.
On middle, on a length. Sarkar taps it late to point and takes a quick single.
On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
On the pads, Sarkar works it towards square leg, they think of one but then opt against it.
Shorter and on middle, Sarkar flicks it to mid-wicket.
On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.
Soumya Sarkar walks out at No.3.

OUT! TAKEN! That is beautifully bowled! The dangerous Das is out of here! Did not look at his best and now falls. Das steps out. Patel slows it up and lands it on off, Das looks to go inside out. The ball turns away at the end, it goes more off the outer half towards point. Scott Kuggeleijn dives to his left and takes a good catch. An early wicket, just what New Zealand needed.
Commentary.Howout: c Scott Kuggeleijn b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: EDGY RUNS! Shorter and outside off, Das looks to cut, it goes off the outside edge fine on the off side for two.
Ajaz Patel is back on.
Just the 6 from the over then! Outside off, it is guided to point.
Gets the length right this time! Tosses it up on middle, it is pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! This time he nails it! This is shorter and Naim has enough time to go back and hammer it through mid-wicket.
Slightly shorter, skids through, hence, the pull is not off the middle, it goes through mid-wicket for two.
Another one outside off, Naim looks to cut but misses.
Shorter and outside off, it is cut to point.
Cole McConchie is into the attack.
Around off, this is guided through point for one.
Short and outside off, Naim slashes at it but misses.
WIDE! Quite wayward! Down the leg side and short. Left alone.
Really good fielding! Fuller and on the pads, Das flicks it towards mid-wicket, the fielder dives to his right and stops it. Just the one.
FOUR! Easy pickings for Das! On the pads, he works it through square leg for the first boundary for Das.
Another one on off, this is also guided down to third man for one.
Outside off, this is guided down to third man for one.
Floats it up on off, it is pushed down to long off for one.
Another one floated up on off, kept out.
On off, this is pushed to cover.
Fired into the pads, Das looks to defend but misses to get hit on the pads.
Slows it up and lands it on middle, it is pushed back to the bowler.
Shorter and outside off, this is cut but to point.
Ajaz Patel to bowl from the other end.
In the air...Safe! A full ball, on middle. Naim flicks it uppishly and towards mid-wicket. The fielder carries it on a bounce. Two taken.
A full ball, on middle. Das tucks it to square leg for a quick single. He is off the mark as well.
Touch short, on middle, flicked to mid-wicket for a single.
A slower short ball, outside off. Naim pulls it to mid off.
Short in length, angling in, on middle. Blocked out.
FOUR! Boundary to start the chase! A full ball, outside off. Naim opens the face of his bat and carves it through point for a boundary. Bangladesh are off the mark.
